correctness.rationale: For nonidentity h, every h-cycle admits at least one-third as many disjoint directed edges as vertices. The three independent subset bits B(x)=1,A(x)=0,A(hx)=1 prohibit commutation with probability 1/8 on each chosen edge. Every nonidentity label pair is thus bounded by 4^n(7/8)^(n/3). Identity labels contribute exactly 4^n. Exactly 2^(n+1)-1 empty-domain pairs per label pair are duplicated and a single zero is restored, giving the nonnegative correction. The finite sandwich and the conditional idempotent concentration follow with explicit quantifiers. The n=1 case is included. Direct full-map multiplication corroborated n=1,2,3,4,6 including S3; numerical checks are not used to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: A quantitative uniform estimate for all finite groups establishes an unexpectedly structure-independent inverse-square commutativity law for the inverse monoids of their regular actions; it also bounds the conditional probability of two partial identities among commuting pairs. This separates group-unit commutativity from monoid commutativity and extends strictly beyond a single 2-group exact census. The assertion is a complete theorem over a naturally motivated all-group family, not a numerical example or merely a restatement of a construction.
